アンソロピックの最先端AIが直面する「安全」と「コスト」のジレンマ 電撃停止が揺るがす上場への成長モデルと、エージェント台頭による企業負担の増大《小久保 重信》@skokubo
米AI新興のアンソロピックによる「Claude Fable（クロード・フェイブル）5」の一般公開は、最先端AIの社会実装がはらむ構造的なジレンマを浮き彫りにした。
同モデルは高い処理能力を示す一方、安全対策の不備を突いた米政府の輸出規制により、公開からわずか3日で電撃的な提供停止に追い込まれる事態となった。
事態はその後、一部モデルの制限解除へと動いたものの、最先端AIのビジネスモデルは依然として深いジレンマの中にある。
また、競合を上回る高額な利用料金は、早期の提供再開を目指す同社にとっても、導入を見据える企業にとってもコスト面の新たな障壁となる。
開発スピードと安全性、経済性のバランスを巡り、最先端AIのビジネスモデルは新たな課題に直面している。
アンソロピックは6月9日、高度なサイバー防御や創薬支援の能力を持つモデル、フェイブル5の一般提供を開始した。
同モデルは、同社が一般公開するには危険すぎると判断していた「Mythos（ミュトス）」を基盤としている。

data.text:
The bottleneck in agentic coding just moved from the model to the harness.

Cognition shipped Devin Fusion today. The mechanism is not model routing. Not picking one model for the entire task. A sidekick architecture: a frontier model runs the session, both models maintain their own cached context, and the frontier model decides what to delegate in real time. Handoffs happen during context compaction, avoiding cache misses entirely.

The numbers on FrontierCode Extended: Fusion plus Fable 5 matches pure Fable 5 performance at 41% lower cost. Without Fable 5, suspended since June 12 per a US government export control directive, Fusion matches Opus and GPT-5.5 at 35% lower cost. 88% of Cognition's internal merged PRs ran through the automated router with no human override.

The task breakdown reveals the actual rule. Mechanical work delegates cleanly: lint fixes, test runs, rote refactors. One javascript refactor delegated the slow test suite and cut cost 62% at no quality loss. Judgment-heavy work backfires. A TypeScript feature with subtle intent requirements scored 27 via sidekick versus 54 solo. The sidekick needs to know what it cannot do.

Harness engineering research this spring shows evolved scaffolds cut token usage by 12% on SWE-bench Verified without changing the base model. Claude Opus 4.8 sits at 88.6% on SWE-bench Verified. Devin's PR merge rate is 67%, up from 34% a year ago. The gains are coming from harness improvements, not just raw model capability.

The frame I keep returning to: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codeium, Claude Code, and Devin are all building proprietary scaffolds on top of the same frontier APIs. Fable 5 inside the Fusion harness scored 57.6 on FrontierCode. Opus 4.8 alone scored 48.8 at higher cost. The model is a commodity input. The harness is the product.

data.text:
$claude, $anthropic The CA–Anthropic deal reads like a SaaS discount story. It isn't. It's Anthropic's first visible step from model layer → orchestration layer in 2B2G — and that's where durable rent actually lives.

The model layer is the shortest-duration moat in AI: frontier leads get matched in quarters. Real durability comes from converting a fleeting model lead into switching costs before the lead erodes.

Watch the structure: a shared-services procurement portal (SITeS), 50% discount, and a state-built orchestration shell (Poppy). Surface-read: buyer guarding against vendor lock-in. But weak public buyers can't actually build or maintain orchestration alone — which turns "buyer-built" into a Forward-Deployed-Engineer entry point, not a defense. This is the Palantir playbook's opening move.

The prize isn't the smartest model. It's welding Claude into low-digitization, high-red-tape government systems. That switching cost is rooted in org inertia + political accountability, NOT technology — so it survives the one thing that dissolves ordinary integration moats: models getting good enough to integrate themselves.

Key tension to track: the same frontier capability that pries open these systems is also what can detonate Anthropic's longest-duration asset — trust/compliance access (see Mythos/Fable suspension). Capability opens the window; safety positioning is what they bank during it.

Not investable directly (still private). But it reprices the whole 2B2G AI stack — and tells you which layer to underwrite when it is. Watch FDE-type hiring and contract language shifting from "subscription" to "custom deployment."

「最も賢いモデルを、全てのタスクに使う必要はない」

生成AIが当たり前になるほど、静かに膨らんでいくのが『トークンコスト』です。米Gartnerによれば、AIインフラの効率化でモデル単価そのものは下がっていく一方、チャット型AIの5〜30倍ものトークンを消費するAIエージェントの普及によって、企業が支払う推論の総コストはむしろ増えていく見通しとのこと。「安くなったはずなのに、請求額は増えている」という逆転現象です。

日本でも帝国データバンクの調査では、小規模企業を中心にAIのコスト負担が課題として挙がりもはや『経営課題』として認識され始めています。

ではどう抑えるか。Anthropicの「Claude Platform」担当のアンジェラ・ジャン氏とケイトリン・レス氏が、実践的な2つの手法を語っていたので整理してみます📝

■ 手法1：AIを「先生と生徒」に分ける
ひとつ目は『アドバイザー戦略』。高性能モデルを「アドバイザー（先生）」、安価なモデルを「エグゼキューター（生徒）」として組み合わせる手法です。
・基本は安いモデルが作業を実行
・判断に迷ったときだけ、高性能モデルに助言を求める
・結果として、安価なモデル単体よりも高い精度を実現

レス氏いわく「アドバイザー戦略を使えば、最先端モデル相当の性能をはるかに安く実現できる」とのこと。肝は、タスクの難易度に応じて段階的に組み合わせることです。

・最難関：Fable 5（先生）×Opus（生徒）
・中程度：Opus（先生）×Sonnet（生徒）
・軽い処理：Sonnet×Haiku 4.5

ここでいう「難しい問題」とは、大規模なレガシーシステムの移行、膨大なデータ処理、影響範囲の広い脆弱性調査、ゲーム開発のような工程の多い案件などを指すそうです。いずれもSIerの現場が日々向き合っているテーマばかり。なお、最上位モデルをアドバイザーに据えれば、実行役が下位モデルでも長時間タスクの処理能力は維持される、という説明も印象的でした。

■ 手法2：プロンプトキャッシングで賢く入力する
ふたつ目は『プロンプトキャッシング』。システムプロンプトやツール指定、メッセージ履歴など、リクエストの冒頭で毎回繰り返す部分をキャッシュし、再処理コストを省く仕組みです。

具体的な料金感は次の通り。
・Opus 4.8の通常入力：100万トークンあたり10ドル
・キャッシュ書き込み（5分保持）：6.25ドル
・キャッシュヒット（2回目以降）：わずか0.5ドル
初回こそ書き込みの追加料金がかかるものの、2回目以降は通常入力の20分の1。社内規定を毎回参照する問い合わせbotや、同じ長文ドキュメントを扱うシステムのように「冒頭が毎回同じ」用途ほど、効果は跳ね上がります。

デフォルトの保持時間は5分ですが、追加料金で1時間まで延ばせるため、アクセスが断続的に続くサービスとも相性が良さそうです。先のアドバイザー戦略と組み合わせれば、削減効果はさらに積み上がります。

■ いま伝えたいこと
ここまで整理して感じたのは、これはまさにSIerや社内開発の腕の見せどころだということ。

「とりあえず一番強いモデルで」という発想は、もはやコスト面で通用しません。求められるのは、業務フローをタスク単位に分解し、それぞれの難易度に最適なモデルを割り当てる『設計力』です。そしてこの設計力こそ、これまでシステムのアーキテクチャを描いてきたエンジニアが最も得意とするところ。SIerにとっては「AI導入で仕事が消える」どころか、コスト設計という新しい付加価値を提案できる好機とも言えます。

つまりAIコストの最適化は、単なる節約術ではなく、設計力がそのまま利益率に直結する新しい競争領域です。最強のモデルを選べる時代だからこそ、あえて選ばない判断にこそ価値が宿る。モデル選びは、性能比較からコスト設計へ。

Anthropic is re-negotiating its partnership with Amazon. Amazon will now pay for Claude based on tokens rather than computing hours, increasing its total bill. You may recall that Fable was pulled after the government was warned of its cyber capabilities by Amazon CEO Andy Jassy.

California Gov. Newsom announces a partnership with Anthropic where state agencies and local governments will get access to Claude (presumably including Mythos/Fable) with a 50% discount. Newsom specifically mentioned strengthening cybersecurity, continuing a trend of government officials becoming concerned with cyber-risk post-Mythos.

I think too many people see AI labs as just the models.

The model matters, obviously. But the better question is who controls the stuff around it: compute, power, data, distribution, products people use, government relationships, and the ability to wire all of that together without lighting the company on fire.

At some point the model starts to look like the UI for the utility underneath.

So unfortunately, I have to talk about Factorio.

If you’ve never played Factorio, it’s just Minecraft for people who think the fun part is supply chains. You crash on a planet, mine rocks, build machines to mine, build machines to build, and eventually build the factory that builds factories.

The game is bottlenecks. You fix iron, then power breaks. You fix power, then throughput breaks. You fix throughput, then some tiny thing three screens away is starving the whole factory.

That is the AI race now.

So, rough map of the factory floor.

1/ OpenAI has the default app. ChatGPT was the first real AI product people used, and when someone says AI, a lot of them still mean ChatGPT. Monster advantage. The problem is the factory still depends on someone else’s infrastructure, particularly Microsoft. Stargate is the attempt to own more of the power bill, but it can also become partner spaghetti around one insane product.

2/ Anthropic has taste. Claude is still the model I trust most when the work requires taste instead of horsepower: intent understanding, steerability, the feeling that it wants to work with you. But trust does not magically buy power. The model serious teams trust can still get outscaled by someone with a wider resource base.

Also, the Fable mess was a reminder that government is now part of the game, not adjacent to it.

3/ Google should be absolutely destroying this. They have TPUs, Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Gmail, Docs, Cloud, distribution to billions of humans, and more data than anyone wants to admit. If Gemini, Workspace, Search, Cloud, YouTube, and dev tools ever feed the same system, everyone should be terrified. If not, every keynote stays a little bit “wait, which product is this in again?”

4/ Meta, Meta, Meta. With Llama, Meta is trying to make its defaults everyone’s defaults. In open source, defaults are power. The play is probably smart: give everyone the ecosystem, keep the sharpest edge for yourself, and hope open source doesn’t commoditize the thing you’re trying to win. Very Zuck, and probably underrated.

5/ xAI and Elon are where this gets messy. The obvious take is “Grok is behind, therefore xAI is behind.” Maybe, if this is only a chatbot race. But if the AI race is Factorio, Grok might be the wrong thing to judge. X gives him messy human feedback and distribution, Tesla gives him cars, batteries, factories, robots, and a path to embodiment, SpaceX gives him satellites, defense relevance, and government relationships, Colossus gives him data-center execution, and xAI gives him the model. None of this automatically composes, and because it is Elon the factory might just be five burning factories in a trench coat. But if it does compose, the upside is not “Grok gets a little better.” It is that the weird pieces start feeding each other.

That is not a chatbot company. That is a factory.

Soooo just Factorio.

The smartest model matters. It’s just not the whole game...just like Factorio

𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐬

Probably the biggest topic the past two weeks have been the takedown and usage of Anthropic’s Fable 5 AI model.

Every AI creator has spoken about how its been banned in and outside of the country due to “security” concerns by the government.

People got depressed.

Even Theo (of T3 chat) who is reputedly “Anthropics #1 hater” subscribed to two Claude Max accounts just to use Fable when it was out.

Because Fable was genuinely good.

Now, its gone.

But then came https://t.co/x0J9hgvlrt, who released the latest in their flagship GLM model, GLM 5.2.

An open weight model that in many people’s opinions (including myself) performs much better in actual real life tasks than Opus 4.8.

GLM 5.2 was - and is - very well received by everyone.

People applauded how far open source has come in catching up to the big boys.

For a moment, there was morale.

Then morale came crashing back down again because OpenAI wanted to release GPT 5.6 which is reportedly 𝑒𝑣𝑒𝑛 𝑏𝑒𝑡𝑡𝑒𝑟 than Fable 5.

But they can’t because, well, 𝑠𝑒𝑐𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑠.

So Anthropic has not only gotten their models become exclusive, now they’ve have - once again - forced everyone to follow their lead.

Including making their #1 rival’s newest best model banned.

The space is rife with opinions.

- “Anthropic has been asking for government regulation, so now they got it! Serves them right!”
- “This isn’t actually a security thing, this is just an excuse to suppress people!”
- “The tech bros are looking to control WHO gets the tech - look, only a FEW companies gets the model!”

Just thinking about this makes me mad.

I like Anthropic’s models.

But I don’t like Anthropic.

More specifically, the kinds of practices that they do.

And I fear what this means to the rest of us if more and more of these practices become commonplace.

I’ve been saying for some time now that the age of AI subsidy is coming to an end.

That people should be taking advantage of this moment to build for when all this is over, when the latest models are exclusive only to a select few.

But my warnings have fallen on deaf ears and people are still going around doing what they do, the way they’ve always done it (without AI).

And now, more proof is coming out on how big tech is going to play this.

- First, they made you fall in love with their products.
- Second, they get you so dependent on their products, that it is too costly to leave.
- Third, they introduce more powerful and expensive models (2-3x more expensive).
- Fourth, they quietly make their older models - the one you’re used to - dumber.
- Fifth, they pull stunts like these to hype things up, raise share prices, and make their best models only available to a select few, making the government throw regulations to limit it even further.
- Finally, they deprecate older models entirely so you are either stuck paying only premium, or stuck with bad models that can’t do a fraction of what the premium ones can do.

This is why so many people are mad.

Big tech is moving the world around like chess pieces, and the public don’t seem to know or care to learn.

Most are still in denial.

A new phrase has come out a few months ago, and has been steadily gaining popularity.

The 𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑢𝑛𝑑𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑙𝑎𝑠𝑠.

A separation between the haves and the have nots.

Except this is no longer referring to wealth, but intelligence.

If you are one of the few, you get to have access to intelligence.

If you are not, you are stuck with mainstream AI.

Yes, it is expected that the impact of having the next gen AI is larger than ‘generational wealth.’

And yes, the difference between mainstream AI and the kind of AIs that are about to take over in the next few years is 𝑡ℎ𝑎𝑡 𝑙𝑎𝑟𝑔𝑒.

If you think that the wealth gap is huge now, whatever the difference is, that may be less than a fraction of what it might be in the next decade or so.

But the story isn’t over.

We are in a crossroads right now and we need to take advantage of this moment.

We are STILL in a place where we get to decide how the future goes.

The actions we take right now, collectively, will not only impact us and our children - but their children’s children and the rest after.

This is why I’m writing this today.

Build stuff.

Take this moment to learn and experiment to see where AI and agents can take you and your business.

Mess around and make mistakes.

The way things are right now, we can STILL afford it.

Because AI will never again be as cheap as they are today.

And if you can, contribute to the open source community.
